what.text: This page follows refugees from Myanmar in Bangladesh, the Rohingya refugee situation; UNHCR counts refugees by country, not by ethnic group, so the figures cover all refugees from Myanmar in Bangladesh.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 1178003, which is 77.3% of all refugees from Myanmar.
Malaysia, Thailand and India are the next largest hosts.

why.text: Myanmar's citizenship law of 15 October 1982 did not list the Rohingya among the recognised national groups, leaving most of them without citizenship.
On 25 August 2017, after attacks by the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) and the military operations that followed, the largest flight of Rohingya to Bangladesh began.
UCDP records armed conflict over Arakan territory with ARSA and ULA from 2016 to 2020, and new armed conflicts after the military seized power on 1 February 2021, including with the NUG.

when.text: UNHCR's series starts in 1978, the year of the first large exodus, at 160000.
A second wave followed in 1991 to 1992, and returns to Myanmar followed from 1993.
The largest recent change came between 2016 and 2017, and the figure was at its highest, 1178003, at the end of 2025.

how.text: UNHCR counts refugees in the camps of Cox's Bazar and on Bhasan Char together, as one national total.
Bangladesh and UNHCR completed a joint registration in Cox's Bazar in 2019, and most refugees received an identity document for the first time.
Bangladesh has not signed the 1951 Refugee Convention, and statelessness is counted in a separate series.
